one_month_reasoning: No Synopsys earnings fall in the window (fiscal Q4 FY26 results are due in early December, after the window). What is in the window: (1) how the stock trades after the 30 Sep/1 Oct investor day, when it rose 12.8% to $490.54 on FY27 guidance well above consensus (revenue $11.10-11.20B, non-GAAP EPS $19.04-19.12 vs $17.81 consensus), an AWS IP deal worth over $1B, an OpenAI revenue share and a ~$1B buyback. Base rates favour mild positive drift after a guidance-driven jump: price targets are moving up (BofA $600, KeyBanc $605, Rosenblatt $620, DB $640, HSBC upgrade to $700) and the buyback adds steady demand. Against that, part of the one-day move may give back, since the stock bounced 35% off its 15 Sep low. (2) The FOMC on 27-28 Oct, the first meeting after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00%; the median dot signals one more 2026 hike (Chase/CNBC) and Polymarket has hold at 74.5%, hike 24.5%. A hike would hit long-duration software multiples, but the hawkish path is already known, so the effect is mostly via a surprise. (3) Cadence Q3 results in late October, read across to the sector. (4) Any new AI-EDA disruption headline like Kimi K3 (Jul/Sep 2026), which has moved both EDA stocks 8-10% in a day. Net: median $494 (slightly above spot), log-sd 12% (about annual vol / 3.75, a bit below 45%/3.5 because there is no earnings event), close to symmetric. Round 2: the supervisor's findings confirm, rather than change, the in-window events, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: Blend of a forward P/E (FY28 non-GAAP EPS ~$22.7 x 24x = $545, weight 0.6) and an FCF multiple (FY28 FCF/share ~$19.7 x 27x = $531, weight 0.4), giving ~$539 twelve months out.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 non-GAAP EPS $22.7 x 24x forward P/E (the multiple the market will apply in Oct 2027)

inputs_detail.derivation: Investor Day framework: ~15% revenue CAGR, ~50% FY30 non-GAAP operating margin, EPS growth in the mid-20s. From FY26 ~$15.07, a 23-25% CAGR implies ~22-24% a year after FY27.

$19.08 x 1.19. The non-GAAP interest expense (~$460M) is already in the FY27 guide (src 19), so I narrow my round-1 haircut from 18% to 19% growth; I still stay below the ~22-24% framework pace for execution risk (2025 IP miss, AI-disruption scares). The framework pace would give ~$23.3-23.7.

Measured on one-year-forward EPS, SNPS was ~40x in Oct 2024 ($513.6 vs FY25 EPS $12.91), ~30x in Oct 2025 ($453.8 vs FY26 guide ~$15.07) and is ~25.7x now on FY27 guide. That is a steady de-rating. Cadence trades at ~43x its 2026 EPS guide ($350.7 / $8.10). With the Fed having hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and the median dot at 4.1% for end-2026 and end-2027 (src 20, 21) and an AI-disruption overhang, I assume the multiple stops falling but does not recover: 24x.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF $3.72B / ~189M diluted shares = $19.7 per share x 27x P/FCF

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 guide $3.1B (src 19) grown 20%. The framework targets FCF growth in the mid-20s FY26-30 (src 19); from FY26 ~$2.6B (src 1) a 25% CAGR reaches ~$6.3B in FY30, i.e. ~27%/yr after FY27. FY27 guide itself is +19% on FY26. I use 20% for FY28: above my round-1 16%, which sat below even the FY27 step-up, but below the framework pace for execution risk.
FY27 guide uses 190-192M (src 19); ~$1B of near-term buybacks plus up to 50% of FCF returned (src 19) at ~$500-550, net of stock-comp dilution, gives ~189M by FY28.
Today the stock is ~30x FY27 FCF by market cap ($490.54 x 191M / $3.1B); the Fool cites just over 25x. I take 27x, a mid-point that allows for net debt of ~$6.4B (src 1).

bear.story: Another AI-disruption scare (Kimi K3-style demo: SNPS -7.8% in a day), tighter China export curbs (9.9% of 9M FY26 revenue), a Design IP miss at the December print or an adverse turn in the class action, with the Fed delivering the signalled extra hike, pushes the multiple to ~17-18x FY28 EPS. 2025-26 had three 30%+ drawdowns, so this is not a tail case.

base.story: Synopsys meets or slightly beats FY27 guidance ($19+ EPS, $11.1B+ revenue, ~$3.1B FCF), FY28 tracks close to the framework (EPS ~$22.7, FCF ~$3.7B), and with rates held at ~4% the forward multiple stops de-rating at ~24x. Buybacks help.

bull.story: AI-agent EDA monetisation (OpenAI, AWS) and verification demand lift growth to the framework pace or above (FY28 EPS ~$23.5); the stock re-rates toward 30x, closing part of the gap to Cadence, in line with HSBC's $700 target. Requires the rate path to stop tightening.

thesis_break_reason: $370 is about the September 2026 panic low ($362.55), set before management guided FY27 EPS to ~$19. Trading there would mean under 20x guided EPS and ~22x guided FCF, most likely signalling the guide is not credible (an IP/China miss, AI tools taking share, an Ansys integration problem) rather than ordinary volatility. I keep $370 rather than the supervisor's $365: the difference is immaterial, and a close back at the pre-guide panic zone already breaks the thesis.

reasoning: Base rates: from monthly closes 2015-2026 (Twelve Data), SNPS's 12-month log return averaged +21% (sd 22%) over 10 years but only +10% (sd 23%) over the last 5, with 35% of rolling windows negative. The long-run drift came largely from multiple expansion, which has reversed: one-year-forward P/E fell from ~40x (Oct 2024) to ~30x (Oct 2025) to ~25.7x today. Annualised monthly vol is 34% (5y) and 39% (2y), realised 1-year vol 45%, so I keep a 12-month log-sd of 0.35 above the median and 0.40 below for a fatter left tail. Since mid-2025 the stock has had three 30%+ drawdowns (IP guide cut, China curbs, AI-disruption scares). Round 2: the supervisor confirmed from primary press that the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 with the median dot at 4.1% for end-2026 and end-2027; I verified this on the J.P. Morgan/Chase summary and now cite it instead of Polymarket alone. That confirms, rather than changes, my no-re-rating 24x exit multiple. I dropped the thin Polymarket recession market ($9.7k volume) as evidence. I re-read the Investor Day release: FCF growth target is mid-20s FY26-30 and the ~$460M non-GAAP interest cost is already in the FY27 guide, so my round-1 FY28 haircuts (16% FCF, 18% EPS) were too harsh; I now use 20% FCF growth ($3.72B) and 19% EPS growth ($22.7), still below the framework. Fair value rises from $530 to $539 (P/E $545 x0.6, FCF $531 x0.4). I raise the median from $515 to $520 (+6%), still below fair value because of the de-rating pattern, a Fed that is still tightening, the Nov 4 class-action response and the December print as the first test of the guide. The ladder gives P(>=491) 0.557, P(>=343) 0.85 and an expected value of about $540. Analyst targets of $600-700 are evidence of upside skew, not the anchor. Research was limited: round 1 about 12 queries plus Twelve Data history; round 2 two page fetches (Investor Day release, Chase FOMC summary; CNBC page was not fetchable).
